narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 52.8% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability tipped just above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three aspects of your academic record. Your class ranking in your third year of law school was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Standing in only the second decile, noticeably below the average of roughly sixth-decile performance among accepted students, signaled to the model a higher risk of struggling on the bar. Your first-year ranking in the third decile reinforced this concern, though it carried less weight than the third-year result.

Surprisingly, your undergraduate GPA of 3.10 worked in the opposite direction. While slightly below the 3.23 average of accepted applicants, it still provided a modest push toward a passing outcome. However, this positive influence was not large enough to overcome the two class-rank signals.

Taken together, the model concluded that your academic trajectory made success on the bar exam more likely to be difficult than not. 

To improve your chances, focus on strengthening your academic performance and consider targeted bar-preparation resources before reapplying. Raising your class standing in future semesters and boosting your LSAT score could meaningfully shift future predictions in your favor.
